metadata.description: Golden dataset for science MCQ evaluation - Chapter 6
metadata.source: Curated from Kaggle LLM Science Exam dataset (train.csv)

changelog.author: evaluation_team
changelog.changes: Initial golden dataset creation from train.csv stratified sample

annotation_guidelines.task_description: For each science MCQ, annotators must select the single best answer from 5 options (A-E)
quality_criteria: Answer must be factually correct based on scientific consensus
If multiple answers seem plausible, choose the most precise/complete one
Mark difficulty level: easy, medium, hard

rubric.correctness: Is the selected answer factually accurate? (required)
rubric.completeness: Does the answer fully address the question? (1-5)
rubric.difficulty: How hard is this for a domain expert? (easy/medium/hard)

items.prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes the impact of Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) on the observed 'missing baryonic mass' discrepancy in galaxy clusters?

choices.A: MOND postulates the existence of fuzzy dark matter.
choices.B: MOND increases the discrepancy from a factor of 10 to 20.
choices.C: MOND explains the mass is in the form of neutrinos and axions.
choices.D: MOND reduces the discrepancy from a factor of 10 to about 2.
choices.E: MOND eliminates the missing mass entirely.

items.prompt: Which of the following is an accurate definition of dynamic scaling in self-similar systems?

choices.A: Evolution of self-similar systems with time-dependent similarity.

items.prompt: What is the term used in astrophysics to describe light-matter interactions resulting in energy shifts in the radiation field?
Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between the dimensions of a diffracting object and the angular spacing of features in the diffraction pattern?

choices.A: Indirectly proportional, smaller object = narrower pattern.
choices.B: Directly proportional, smaller object = narrower pattern.
choices.D: Inversely proportional, smaller object = wider pattern.
choices.E: Proportional to square root, smaller = slightly narrower.

items.prompt: What is the difference between active and passive transport in cells?

choices.A: Both require energy input from the cell.
choices.B: Passive transport is powered by osmosis and electric field; active requires energy input.
choices.C: Passive requires energy; active is powered by osmosis and electric field.
choices.D: Both are powered by osmosis and electric field.
choices.E: Active is powered by osmosis and electric field; passive requires energy.

items.prompt: What is the difference between natural convection and forced convection?

choices.A: Same phenomenon involving fans and density.
choices.C: Natural = density-driven displacement; forced = fans/pumps drive flow.
choices.E: Same phenomenon with both density and fans.

choices.A: Measure of how much a material absorbs magnetization.
choices.B: Measure of how much a material becomes magnetized in an applied field.
choices.C: Measure of how much a material resists magnetization.
choices.D: Measure of how much a material conducts magnetization.
choices.E: Measure of how much a material reflects magnetization.

items.prompt: What is the significance of regularization in terms of renormalization problems in physics?

choices.B: Allows breakdown of a theory with infinite radius.
choices.C: Demonstrates a system below certain size without further calculations.
choices.D: Provides highly accurate description under specific conditions with infinite radius.
choices.E: Explains system operation below certain size with infinite radius.

items.prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes the blocking temperature of an antiferromagnetic layer in a spin valve?

choices.A: Temperature at which magnetization aligns with field, higher than Neel.
choices.B: Temperature below which layer loses ability to pin, higher than Neel.
choices.C: Temperature at which ferromagnetic layer demagnetizes, higher than Neel.
choices.D: Temperature at or above which layer ceases pinning, lower than Neel.
choices.E: Temperature at which ferromagnetic loses pinning ability, higher than Neel.

failure_history.reason: Subtle distinction between B and D

items.prompt: What is the relationship between mass, force, and acceleration, according to Sir Isaac Newton's laws of motion?

choices.A: Mass determines weight; 1kg accelerates at 1 m/s^2 with 1N.
choices.B: Mass is inertial; 1kg accelerates at 10 m/s^2 with 1N.
choices.C: Mass is inertial; 1kg accelerates at 10 m/s^2 with 10N.
choices.D: Mass is inertial; 1kg accelerates at 1 m/s^2 with 1N.
choices.E: Mass determines size; 1kg accelerates at 1 m/s^2 with 10N.

items.prompt: What is the throttling process, and why is it important?

choices.A: Steady flow through resistance; causes pressure increase in refrigerators.
choices.B: Steady adiabatic flow through resistance; causes temperature drop in refrigerators.
choices.C: Steady adiabatic flow through resistance; causes pressure drop in refrigerators.
choices.D: Steady flow through resistance; causes temperature increase in refrigerators.
choices.E: Steady adiabatic flow; not used in refrigeration cycle.

items.prompt: What is the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and how does it relate to angular momentum in quantum mechanics?

choices.A: Axis undefined; particles have spin; tensorial operator in relativistic QM.
choices.B: Total angular momentum equals sum; centre of mass defined.
choices.C: Total angular momentum subject to quantization; expressed as operators.
choices.D: Axis undefined; only one projection measurable; quantized eigenvalues.
choices.E: Only one projection measurable; expressed as operator with quantized eigenvalues.

failure_history.reason: D and E are very similar; subtle distinction

items.prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes the dimension of an object in a CW complex?

choices.A: Largest n for which n-skeleton is nontrivial; empty set has dimension -1.
choices.B: Determined by number of critical points; discrete boundary has dimension 1.
choices.C: Smallest n for which n-skeleton is nontrivial; empty set has dimension -1.
choices.D: Counting cells of all dimensions; empty set has dimension 0.
choices.E: Depends on number of singularities; both empty set and boundary have dimension 0.

items.prompt: What is a uniform tiling in the hyperbolic plane?

choices.A: Tessellation with irregular polygons; not vertex-transitive.
choices.B: Tessellation with regular polygons; not vertex-transitive.
choices.D: Edge-to-edge filling with regular polygons; vertex-transitive and isogonal.
choices.E: Edge-to-edge filling with irregular polygons; vertex-transitive.

items.prompt: What happens to excess base metal as a solution cools from the upper transformation temperature towards an insoluble state?

choices.A: Solidifies as proeutectoid until eutectoid level.
choices.B: Crystallizes-out as proeutectoid until eutectoid level.
choices.C: Dissolves as proeutectoid until eutectoid level.
choices.D: Liquefies as proeutectoid until eutectoid level.
choices.E: Evaporates as proeutectoid until eutectoid level.
